cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description:
The IsOSPlatform determines the build-host OS, not the target OS, so this will be excluded if we build for MacOS on a Windows host.

I prefer a separate folder with the `.c` file and a small shell script that builds the library for x64 and arm64. We can then include the binaries directly in Git, and it is then not a requirement to have `clang` to build the whole solution, only `dotnet`.

evidence.thread_resolution: carljohnsen: Makes sense, I've added a build script, built the library for arm64 and x86_64, combined them into a universal binary. On build they're now copied to `runtimes/osx/native/` and the P/Invoke declarations have been updated to reference the new path. It's [this commit](https://github.com/duplicati/duplicati/pull/6784/commits/5fd62b0fc274c5d0f239d339211d1056c80ae1d1).
